segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So far, in these lectures, we've been looking at crimes like robbery and murder- both from a historical viewpoint and also in contemporary society - and we've seen that the preoccupation in Western society with crime and with lawlessness is part of a long and continuous tradition, rather than something which is new and unique to modern society.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But over the past seventy years or so. there has been a massive increase in one type of crime, which is what's known as 'corporate crime'.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Corporate crime is crime which, as the name suggests, is connected with companies, with business organisations.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It includes illegal acts of either individuals or a group within the company, but what is important is that these acts are normally in accordance with the goals of the company - they're for the good of the company rather than the individual.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It's been defined as, quote, 'crime which is committed for the corporate organisation' - the company - 'not against it', unquote.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So crimes like theft b.y employees- things like embezzlement or fraud against one's actual employer are excluded according to this definition.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The employees may be involved but they're acting in the first place for the company - they may not even realise they're committing a crime or they may realise but they feel it's excusable because it's policy, or because otherwise they may lose their jobs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So here, really, we're talking about the links between power and crime.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, this is one area that much less is generally known about than conventional or traditional crime.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It has been relatively ignored by the mass media- for , it tends to be under-reported in comparison with conventional crime in news broadcasts, and in crime serials and films and so on - they very rarely deal with corporate crime.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And it also tends to be Ignored in academic circles- there's been far more research on conventional crime and far more data is available.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are several reasons for this lack of interest in corporate crime, compared with other types of crime.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It's often very complex, whereas with conventional crime it's usually possible to follow what's going on without specialist knowledge.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As well as this. whereas conventional crime usually has a Jot of human interest, corporate crime often has much less.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The third reason, and possibly the most significant one, is that very often the victims are unaware - they think their misfortune is an accident or that it's the fault of no-one in particular.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They're unaware that they've been victims of a crime.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So, when we look at the effects of corporate crime we may find it's very difficult to assess the costs.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But these costs can be very considerable in both their economic and social aspects.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Let's look at the economic costs first.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For , if a company is producing fruit juice and it dilutes its product so that it's just a little below the concentration it should be, many millions of people may be paying a small amount extra for their carton of orange juice.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now small amounts like this may seem insignificant for individual customers- too small to worry about - but for the company this deception might result in massive illegal profit.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: However, all studies of corporate crime agree that the individuals are in fact deprived of far more money by such crime than they are by conventional crime like robbery and theft.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In addition to this, we have to consider the social costs of corporate crime and these are again very difficult to assess, but they are considerable.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They're important because they can undermine the faith of the public in the business world and also, more importantly, because the main group of people they affect are, in fact, not the richer sections of society but the poorer - so here companies are robbing the poor to benefit the rich.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are two more points to do with corporate crime that I'd like to illustrate with reference to a specific event which occurred several years ago.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This was an explosion of a large oil tanker which caused the loss of more than fifty lives of the crew.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It was an explosion which never should have happened and a subsequent inquiry laid the blame not on anyone who had actually been on the tanker at the time, but on the owners of the tanker.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They had deliberately decided not to carry out necessary repair work on the tanker as it was due to be sold, and it was this lack of repair work which was directly responsible for the explosion.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now this illustrates two points to do with corporate crime.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: First of all. that it does not have to be intentional.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The owners of the tanker certainly did not intend it to explode.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But very serious consequences can result from people or organisations not considering the possible results of their actions seriously enough.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The main crime here was indifference to & the human results rather than actual intention to harm anyone. but that didn't make the results any less tragic.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And this leads me to my second point - that corporate crime can have very severe consequences.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It's not just a matter of companies making bigger profits than they should do, but of events which may affect the lives of innocent people, and yet very often companies, because they say they didn't intend to harm anyone, can avoid taking responsibility for the results of their actions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And that has been a very dangerous loophole in the law.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A further of corporate crime was . . . (fade out)
